events.continuity_hook: Starts a new conference-travel episode after the May client workshop wraps up.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the Chicago trip, identify viable flight windows and hotel areas, and list the event details Maya needs before routing a plan for approval.
events.scenario_brief: After the Raleigh-Durham workshop, Maya is nominated to attend a healthcare interoperability conference in Chicago from Tuesday, June 23 through Friday, June 26. She will book individually and travel solo, with a few coworkers attending on separate itineraries. She wants Atlanta-to-Chicago flights that avoid a punishingly early start, a Friday return after the closing sessions, and a well-reviewed hotel near the conference shuttle route. The organizer has not confirmed whether Monday evening networking is important, the employer hotel block is still partly waitlisted, and it is unclear whether ORD or MDW gives the cleaner trip to the conference area.

events.continuity_hook: Continues Chicago planning after the first required Tuesday session is confirmed.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the main flight-and-hotel combinations and choose the package Maya should send for approval.
events.scenario_brief: The conference agenda now includes a Tuesday 9:00 a.m. implementation roundtable, so Monday arrival is necessary. Flight choices include a Monday late-morning Delta nonstop to ORD that arrives early afternoon, a cheaper one-stop itinerary into MDW that would land near rush hour, and an evening nonstop that would make the first night feel compressed. Friday options include a midafternoon nonstop that works only if she skips informal vendor conversations after the closing session and a later nonstop with more cushion. Hotel choices are the attached conference hotel with strong ratings, on-site dining, and paid breakfast; a nearby suite property with included breakfast but a longer walk or shuttle; and a Loop hotel near restaurants but less convenient for morning sessions. The open question is whether the attached hotel rate will pass manager review.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Chicago episode from comparison to booking after manager approval and a new Friday meeting change.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the Chicago flight timing, hotel booking notes, and seat choices before the fare hold expires.
events.scenario_brief: Maya's manager approves the Monday late-morning nonstop and the attached conference hotel, but the fare hold expires that evening. A product-team meetup has been added Friday from 1:30 to 2:30 p.m., making the midafternoon return too tight unless she leaves early. The later nonstop gets her home later than ideal but avoids a rushed exit and does not require a connection. The hotel can note a quiet room away from elevators, while breakfast remains paid unless she uses nearby cafes. Seat maps show a few window seats left toward the back of the aircraft, with better forward seats mostly aisle or middle.

events.continuity_hook: Final pre-trip check for Chicago after flights, hotel, and Friday timing are settled.
events.interaction_goal: Build a compact Chicago travel checklist and identify the few items Maya should recheck the day before flying.
events.scenario_brief: A week before departure, Maya has the Monday ATL-to-ORD nonstop, the attached conference hotel, and the later Friday return booked. The conference app confirms Monday badge pickup opens at 4:00 p.m. and Tuesday sessions start at 9:00 a.m. A hot, stormy forecast could affect airport transfers, and a large city event may make rideshares more expensive near the hotel. The hotel confirms on-site dining but no included breakfast. Maya wants a final logistics pass covering Atlanta airport timing, ORD-to-hotel transportation, luggage drop, badge pickup, Tuesday morning routing inside the venue, breakfast workarounds, first-night dinner options, receipt handling, and whether any better window seats have opened.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new family leisure episode after the June conference travel block.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the St. Pete family trip, compare airport and hotel-area tradeoffs, and identify what Maya needs to confirm with her spouse.
events.scenario_brief: After returning from the Chicago conference, Maya starts looking at a late-summer family beach trip to St. Pete Beach before school resumes. The tentative window is Wednesday, August 5 through Sunday, August 9, but her spouse may only be able to take Thursday and Friday off. The trip is for three travelers from Atlanta, and she wants simple flights into Tampa or Sarasota, a return that still leaves time to reset at home before Monday, and a hotel or condo-style room that makes beach time, a pool, breakfast or easy groceries, and casual dinners manageable with a child. Early hotel options range from a Gulf-side resort with fees and paid breakfast to a suite property farther inland with included breakfast but less beach convenience. The unresolved pieces are the exact dates, airport choice, whether a rental car is worth it, and whether a balcony or kitchenette matters enough to change the hotel shortlist.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the St. Pete family trip after the spouse narrows the workable dates.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the revised Thursday-to-Sunday flight and hotel combinations and settle on the package Maya should hold or book.
events.scenario_brief: Maya's spouse confirms that Thursday, August 6 through Sunday, August 9 is realistic, while adding Monday would be difficult. ATL-to-Tampa nonstops have the best combination of schedule and fare, while Sarasota flights reduce the drive but cost more and have less convenient times. The easiest outbound is a Thursday morning nonstop that reaches Florida before lunch; the after-work option is cheaper but sacrifices most of the first evening. Sunday return choices include an early afternoon nonstop that feels rushed and a late-afternoon nonstop that still gets everyone home before bedtime. Hotels are narrowed to a Gulf-side property with a pool, nearby restaurants, resort and parking fees, and paid breakfast versus a larger suite hotel about 15 minutes inland with included breakfast and parking. The main decisions are whether beach convenience outweighs the roomier suite, whether to add a rental car, and whether to book before the better cancellable rates disappear.
